html:
The County of Oldenburg was a small state in northwest Germany, between the Weser and the Dutch border. On the map for 1715 it was ruled by the king of Denmark.

Its counts gave their name to one of Europe's great royal houses. In 1448 Count Christian was chosen king of Denmark, and his descendants ruled Denmark-Norway for centuries. When the counts at home died out in 1667, Oldenburg passed to the Danish king, who ruled it from Copenhagen. In 1773 Denmark traded it to the Gottorp branch of the family in a deal with Russia, and in 1774 it became a duchy. It later became a grand duchy and lasted, in the end as a German state, until 1946. Its neighbour to the east was Hanover, within the Holy Roman Empire.
